title: Optimize / Evals 1:1 follow-up - quality regression & A/B notes
notes:
Meeting: 1:1 follow-up on Optimize / Evals review (quick sync)
Date: 2026-03-10
Attendees: Samir, Jamie, Olivia (notes)
Context: After the 2026-03-08 canary we started seeing a measurable quality regression on promptset-v2 (customer-facing QA prompts). Baseline -> current A: pass@threshold dropped ~4.2% overall; concentrated in 'instruction-follow' and 'few-shot-code' slices. A/B was running model variant m-redwood-1.4 + int8 quant vs baseline m-redwood-1.3 + q4_0.
Observed signals:
- Aggregate metrics: pass_rate down 4.2%, BLEU-ish/EM-like metrics down 3-5 points on subset.
- User-facing examples: increased hallucination in knowledge-heavy prompts, and truncated outputs on long-context code completions.
- Telemetry: KV cache miss-rate slightly higher on canary nodes; tail-latency spike correlated with some cache miss/rebuild events.
- Deployment: Canary at 15% traffic; rollout paused once regression flagged by eval alert.
Initial hypotheses (brainstorm):
1) Quantization profile mismatch for certain layers causing under-generation or token collapse in some examples.
2) Tokenization change (tokenizer update between 1.3 -> 1.4) altering prompt boundaries for few-shot templates.
3) KV cache eviction bug introduced in new runtime kernel optimizing for memory (explains tail-latency and truncation).
4) Decoding defaults changed (top-p/top-k or sampling temp) in serving config for m-redwood-1.4 variant.
5) Evaluation harness seeded differently or metric computation changed (sanity-check the eval pipeline).
Quick checks we agreed to run immediately:
- Re-run eval-suite on canary logs with fixed random seed + deterministic decoding to rule out metric harness flakiness.
- Compare tokenization diffs on a failing example between 1.3 and 1.4 locally (token sequences + offsets).
- Run a focused A/B with identical decode config but swapped quantization (m-redwood-1.4 w/ old quant profile) to isolate quantization impact.
- Sample traces for KV cache lifecycle on canary nodes around observed truncations.
- Generate per-slice diffs and top-20 worst examples (for product team review).
Unresolved questions / decisions to make:
- If quantization is root cause, do we pin older quant profile for canary until we fix the quant step? (lean: yes, pin and block rollout)
- Do we need immediate rollback of canary? We have pause in place; rollback only if re-run confirms persistent regression across deterministic runs.
- Who owns the kernel/runtime trace analysis? (SRE + serving-runtime to pair)
Notes to self: keep communication short to PMs + CS; share top-20 fails + short writeup. Flag enterprise customers on Dedicated if they could be affected (filter by model routing).
